name: text-styles
title: Text styles specimen
summary: A type specimen: thin, light, regular, bold and black weights, italic and bold italic, letter spacing 0 and 0.25 em, and one paragraph at line heights 1.0 and 1.6.
prompt: Make a typography specimen showing font weights from thin to black, italic, letter spacing and line height on a paragraph.
teaches: Set a text's weight with fontWeight, a number from 100 (thin) to 900 (black); 400 is regular (the default) and 700 bold
Slant a text with fontStyle "italic", alone or with a bold fontWeight
Spread letters apart with letterSpacing, in em (0.25 is a quarter of the font size)
Open up a wrapped paragraph with lineHeightMultiplier (1.0 is the default, 1.6 airy), and give a text its own background and padding through its modifiers

snippets.note: paragraph with lineHeightMultiplier 1.6, background and padding as text modifiers

check.describe: Five lines grow from thin to black weight; two italic lines lean; the second TRACKING line is wider than the first and the second paragraph's lines sit further apart than the first's (the C++ screenshot does not show these two yet: EXAMPLES_FINDINGS C13). Resized: at 240 wide the paragraphs rewrap and the specimen grows taller than the screen, and at 360×340 it is cut at the bottom: the column scrolls vertically (verticalScroll) instead of overflowing.

pitfalls: fontStyle takes "italic" (or 1); bold is not a style, it is fontWeight 700
letterSpacing is in em, not dp: 0.25 at fontSize 18 adds 4.5 dp per letter, and 2 would be enormous
lineHeightMultiplier only shows on text that wraps onto several lines: give the text a bounded width (fillMaxWidth) so it wraps
A font renders only the weights it has: on a system font with few weights neighbouring values (500 and 600, say) can look the same
A specimen or settings page is taller than a short or narrow screen: give the root column a verticalScroll so the rest can be reached
